title: My Heart Lies When It Loves You
text:
My heart lies when it loves you,

made faithful interpreter of my sense,

like the echo perceived in an abyss

that the wind, not the voice, forms and spills.


This imperious longing that claims you

was not nourished in the center of the soul:

it has troubled me without myself, like sound,

foreign to my being, like flame.


When the blood saturates the heart

with only your flavor-a middle term

in a mad syllogism of bitterness-,


inaccessible to the implacable siege,

like a piece of lead in dark water,

the soul sinks into silent tedium.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the scholastic bitterness of echo, flame, syllogism, and the soul sinking like lead.

title: The Second Song of Shulamite
text:
Let me know, Love, where you pasture,

where you guide your flocks, where you wander,

lest I tread after the ill-fated islands

the ashen routes of evening.


Your flock, O tender Love, where do you sustain it

and delight it with richest pastures,

while you threaten my clumsy heart

with long paths and slow hours?


Let me not begin to follow the shepherds'

scattered flocks. My life,

show, far away, the sun of your loves;


tell me where you pasture still!,

and I will follow your trace and your scents

through the fires of golden noon.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Song of Songs pastoral search and the final trail of scent through noon.

title: I Want to Say That I Love You and I Do Not Say It
text:
I want to say that I love you and I do not say it,

though I well feel my heart wounded,

because, to my sorrow, I have proven

that I am a lukewarm lover and a weak friend.


Not loving you more is guilt and punishment,

for you have burned me with longings for your love,

and merely by leaving me in my sin

you make your severity toward me extreme.


I only want to live in order to seek you,

I only fear dying before finding you,

I only feel alive when I call you;


and though I live burning in living fire,

because I deny you my whole will,

I do not dare to tell you that I love you.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the devotional paradox of loving, seeking, and withholding the whole will.

title: Jezebel
text:
Pallor consummated in desire,

sum of transparent and delicate flesh,

already sealed, in prophetic routine,

for the soldier and for the Hebrew dog.


O hopeless fever, O delirium

that swings like a pendulum in ruin,

from a vineyard the sun pampers and strikes down

to bloody glory and military trophy!


Horror of pause and silence, perhaps

so as not to know the turbid races

of the heart toward the fatal sunset,


nor feel that in its treacherous valves

the blood is already sweetening step by step

to flatter the jaws of beasts.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Jezebel image as prophetic body, ruin, blood, and approaching beasts.

title: Let Me Know, Love, Where You Pasture...
text:
Let me know, Love, where you pasture,

where you guide your flocks, where you wander,

lest I tread after the ill-fated islands

the ashen routes of evening.


Your flock, O tender Love, where do you sustain it

and delight it with richest pastures,

while you threaten my clumsy heart

with long paths and slow hours?


Let me not begin to follow the shepherds'

scattered flocks. My life,

show, far away, the sun of your loves;


tell me where you pasture still!,

and I will follow your trace among the flowers,

through the fires of golden noon.
editorial_note: The translation keeps this variant's floral closing distinct from the related Shulamite song.
